summary: Contractors improving or repairing real property do not charge Vermont sales tax to the customer; they pay tax on the materials they buy.

citations.title: VT Dept. of Taxes, Contractors
citations.quote: When contractors incorporate tangible personal property (TPP) into buildings, structures, and landscapes, the contractor should not charge sales tax to the customer.

citations.title: VT Dept. of Taxes, Contractors
citations.quote: Examples of real property improvements include electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, and cooling systems; carpentry; roofing; plastering; foundations; landscaping; and painting.

notes: A retailer or manufacturer that elects to be treated as a retailer when installing goods it sells charges sales tax instead (not this code). Only the current, undated Department page was read, so the rule starts on the day it was read; the treatment is long-standing. Covers improvement and repair alike.

summary: Professional services (legal, accounting, consulting, IT, engineering, design, advertising) are not taxable in Vermont, which taxes only enumerated services.

citations.title: VT Dept. of Taxes Ruling 2009-06 (September 4, 2009)
citations.quote: Vermont does not have a broad-based tax on services and thus only those services that are specifically enumerated in the statute are subject to tax.

citations.title: VT Dept. of Taxes Ruling 2024-08 (December 16, 2024)
citations.quote: This is a service that is not taxable in Vermont, even if you utilize taxable software to assist you in providing these services.

notes: The taxable services in 32 V.S.A. § 9771 are utilities, fabrication, admissions, telecommunications and similar; none of the seven professional subcodes. Ruling 2009-06 found help-desk and monitoring services untaxed; Ruling 2024-08 found tax preparation untaxed. Software and goods sold with a service are taxable on their own.

summary: Custom changes to prewritten software, charged separately and reasonably, are exempt from Vermont sales tax.

notes: The code's 'charged separately' meets the condition. Earliest date: the software page describes the law from 2024-07-01; earlier text not read.

summary: Prewritten software delivered on media or electronically is taxable in Vermont at 6%.

citations.quote: Effective July 1, 2024, all sales of prewritten computer software are subject to sales and use tax, including software purchased on storage media, downloaded to a computer system, or accessed remotely via the internet.

notes: Earliest dated text read: Ruling 2009-06. Remote access (SaaS) is the separate code.

notes: Vermont's local option taxes are separate: the 1% local option sales tax (carried in the rate data as the local part where levied) and a 1% local option meals tax that some towns levy instead or as well (a different list of towns). notes: Vermont's local option taxes are separate: the 1% local option sales tax (carried in the rate data as the local part where levied) and a 1% local option meals tax that some towns levy instead or as well (a different list of towns). For a taxable meal the local part is the meals tax, not the sales tax: 1% where the town levies the local option meals tax, nothing where it levies only the sales tax. Known gap: a town that levies only the local option meals tax has no local part in the rate data, so its 1% on meals is missed.
